A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research, with IndicSuperTokenizer renamed MUTANT-Indic and presented within the MUTANT recipe. The complete main texts and appendices, including figures, tables, and equations, support comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original tokenizer benchmarks, downstream evaluations of trained models, inference measurements, continual-pretraining experiments, and ablations.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds Stage-1 downstream evaluations, bits-per-character results, and measured morphology-aware tokenization throughput.

M1.justification: The implemented tokenizer retains the two-stage BPE curriculum, 180K-to-200K vocabulary transition, LLaMA-4 pre-tokenization, NFKC normalization, and sentence-boundary constraints. The MUTANT framing and fuller curation and regex descriptions do not establish a changed algorithm; the tokenizer-replacement procedure also remains unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions cover the same 22 Indic languages, English, code, and downstream benchmark families. The added BPC evaluations reuse existing benchmarks, and the Hindi timing experiment extends the existing morphology analysis without establishing new language, domain, or task coverage.

E2.justification: v2 adds a Stage-1-only model to downstream comparisons in Table 26 while retaining the nine public tokenizer baselines. The BoundlessBPE-style IST-BR comparator survives as 'Single-stage' in Table 12, but its NSL row from v1 Table 21 is absent from v2 Table 22.

E3.justification: v2 introduces BPC scoring of gold-answer continuations, a Stage-1-only downstream evaluation, and tokenizer throughput measurement on approximately 4–5 MB of Hindi text. Existing model sizes, pretraining configurations, benchmark shot settings, and the main LLM latency protocol remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 substantially strengthens supplementary analysis through the Stage-1 downstream ablation, BPC diagnostics addressing near-chance accuracy, and a quantitative test of morphology-preprocessing overhead. Existing vocabulary, data-size, transition, normalization, and glitch-token analyses remain. Table 24 redisplays previously reported fertility values; Table 26 supplies genuinely new downstream evidence.

E5.justification: Appendix C.2 newly specifies ten measurement runs and five warm-up runs for the morphology-aware timing experiment. The original LLM latency experiment retains its ten-run protocol and identical TTFT uncertainty values; no increased repetitions, training-seed analysis, confidence intervals, or significance tests are reported.

E6.justification: Substantial new results include BPC comparisons in Tables 20–21, morphology-aware throughput of 90K versus MUTANT-Indic's 194K tokens/s, and Stage-1 downstream scores in Table 26. The latter reports an Indic average of 0.403 versus the retained Stage-2 average of 0.394. Original headline and benchmark values are retained, while the IST-BR NSL results are removed.

T1.justification: The tokenizer formalization and embedding-initialization mathematics are unchanged. v2 supplies a conventional BPC formula to explain its additional evaluation metric, without introducing a theoretical result, substantive derivation, assumption, or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion redefine the central contribution from an Indic-specific tokenizer to MUTANT, a general multilingual tokenizer-design recipe, with MUTANT-Indic as its instantiation. This broadens the claimed contribution beyond renaming, although the headline fertility and throughput claims remain unchanged.

C2.justification: v2 explicitly limits evidence to the evaluated languages and models up to 1B parameters and acknowledges incomplete linguistic coverage of its metrics. It recognizes Stage-1 as a strong baseline, explains BPC's usefulness near chance accuracy, and broadens the recommended transition range from 90% to 85–90% despite unchanged ablation values.

D1.justification: v2 substantially expands documentation of corpus sampling, fastText language identification, MinHash deduplication, HTML and boilerplate filtering, and script validation. Appendices C.4–C.7 add inference-set composition, baseline tokenizer specifications, and explicit Stage-2 boundary handling. These are newly documented details rather than demonstrated changes to retained experiments; artifact release remains promised.

R1.justification: v2 adds references supporting data-mixture discussion, BPC evaluation, and corpus processing, including Hayase, Heineman, FineWeb, Stack v2, and MegaMath. The principal relationship to SuperBPE and BoundlessBPE remains intact, so the literature expansion is limited.

P1.justification: v2 extensively reframes the narrative around a general recipe, rewrites the abstract and contributions, expands and reorders Section 3, and reorganizes related work and evaluation material. It also adds a dedicated limitations section and several appendix subsections, changes terminology, and swaps the metrics and extended-results appendix order.

P2.justification: The document changes from single-column to two-column layout, adds a pipeline diagram, merges three ablation tables into Table 13, relocates normalization results, and adds several tables. Benchmark tables are restructured. New labeling problems include 'Original LLaMA-4' in Table 11 despite its LLaMA-3.2 context and duplicate Stage-1 headers in Table 26.

improvement.justification: The Stage-1 downstream control, BPC diagnostics, and measured morphology overhead make v2's evidence more informative than v1's. Expanded preprocessing details and explicit applicability limits improve transparency. These targeted gains outweigh the new table-labeling errors, although the broader general-recipe claim remains supported by essentially the same Indic-focused, 1B-model experimental scope.
